config_name: XPS 14 — Core Ultra X9 378H, 64GB LPDDR5X, 2TB SSD, 14" QHD+ 2.8K 120Hz touch

specs.cpu: Intel Core Ultra X9 378H (Series 3 Panther Lake, 16-core, top bin)
specs.ports: 3x Thunderbolt 4 (USB-C) with DP 2.1 + PD, universal audio jack
specs.keyboard_notes: Backlit keyboard, zero-lattice design, Gorilla Glass 3 palmrest

battery.notes: 70Wh. Top-bin 378H and 2TB drive draw slightly more; ~10-11.5h real-world mixed estimated.

price.notes: VERIFIED dell.ca 2026-11-24: CAD $7,779.99. No discount shown on this flagship tier.

reviews.quote: It's great to see Dell bring back the XPS and do so with such style.
Matches MacBook Pro in price but not performance

praises: 64GB in a 1.38 kg 14-inch is effectively unique in the Windows market — local LLM and VM users actually shop this SKU
Top-bin Ultra X9 378H is the fastest CPU Dell ships in a consumer clamshell under 16 inches
2TB Gen4 SSD from factory suits creators shooting 4K on the road
Big NPU + Arc iGPU combo gives the best on-device AI capability of the 14 line
Same quiet cooling and premium build owners praise across the line
complaints: $7,780 buys no discrete GPU — at this price a MacBook Pro 14 or RTX-equipped creator laptop outperforms it (CNET's price-vs-performance critique at its worst)
No OLED option on the 14 regardless of price
Thermals: 16-core H-series in a 15 mm chassis throttles on sustained all-core loads vs thicker rivals
Zero upgrade path — the 64GB you buy is all you ever have
No fingerprint reader on a $7.8k machine

design_philosophy: The halo configuration of the XPS 14 line: Dell's answer to 'how much can you stuff into 1.38 kg'. It targets developers and AI-curious creators who need 64GB unified-class memory in x86 Windows without carrying a workstation.
rating_notes: Inferred from CNET XPS 14 (2026) 8.1 anchor: X9 378H top bin + 64GB → productivity +0.5 over 358H tier, ai_ml +1 (64GB memory ceiling for local models), battery −0.5, thermals −0.5 (hottest config in chassis).
